screening.reason: Inclusion 2,3: resting-state fMRI diagnostic classification (ASD vs NC) on ABIDE NYU (primary) and UM (secondary) site subsets using a multi-scale graph convolutional network.

evidence_spans.text: The proposed MGRL is evaluated on 184 subjects from the public Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE) database with rs-fMRI scans.

In this work, we use rs-fMRI data from the New York University (NYU) site with the largest sample size collected in this database. Speciﬁcally, the NYU site includes 184 subjects, 79 of whom were from ASD and 105 NC cases.
evidence_spans.claim: Primary cohort: NYU site, 79 ASD, 105 NC.

evidence_spans.text: the remaining volumes are processed by a well- accepted pipeline with the Data Processing Assistant for Resting- State fMRI toolbox (DPARSF) (Yan et al., 2016).

by partitioning the brain into multiple ROIs using two atlases, i.e., Automated Anatomical Labeling (AAL) (Tzourio-Mazoyer et al., 2002) atlas with 116 ROIs and Craddock200 (CC200) (Craddock et al., 2012) atlas with 200 ROIs.
evidence_spans.claim: Multi-scale atlases: AAL (116 ROIs) and CC200 (200 ROIs).

evidence_spans.text:
Considering the small amount of subjects, we randomly select
80% of all the samples as training data, 10% of all samples as
validation data, and the remaining 10% as test data. We repeat the
random partition process 100 times and record the mean and SD
results of each method.
evidence_spans.claim: Validation: random 80/10/10 train/val/test split repeated 100 times, mean±SD reported.
MGRL main NYU result: accuracy 0.795, recall 0.809, precision 0.823, F1 0.802, AUC 0.886.

evidence_spans.text: to avoid signiﬁcant inter-site heterogeneity, we mainly used rs-fMRI data from the NYU site. While ABIDE contains data from 21 sites, as a future work, we will evaluate the proposed method on all sites in ABIDE and design smart techniques to reduce inter-site data heterogeneity.
evidence_spans.claim: Authors deliberately restricted to single sites (NYU/UM) to avoid inter-site heterogeneity; no multi-site/leave-site-out evaluation performed.

assessments.support: "the NYU site includes 184 subjects, 79 of whom were from ASD and 105 NC cases" with demographic Table 1 (age, sex, FIQ) for both NYU and UM.
DPARSF pipeline fully described (head motion correction, nuisance regression, MNI standardization, band-pass filter) and two atlases (AAL, CC200) specified with ROI counts.
ASD/NC labels taken from the ABIDE phenotype file; the specific diagnostic instrument/criteria are not elaborated in this paper.

Validation uses a randomized 80/10/10 split repeated 100 times with mean±SD (addresses single-split uncertainty), but sites are evaluated separately rather than pooled with site covariate/harmonisation or leave-site-out, and it is not stated whether feature normalization/graph construction was confined to the training partition within each repeat.

risk_of_bias.summary: Cohort, pipeline and atlases are clearly reported with repeated random-split validation giving uncertainty estimates; residual concerns are an unstated diagnostic-instrument source and unclear confinement of preprocessing/feature steps to training folds.

charting.specific_features: Multi-scale functional connectivity networks (Pearson correlation) using AAL (116 ROIs) and CC200 (200 ROIs) atlases
charting.specific_algorithms: MGRL (multi-scale graph representation learning, dual GCN branches with feature fusion), compared against DCF, LCCF, CCF, GCNA (single-scale AAL GCN), GCNC (single-scale CC200 GCN)
charting.validation_methodology: Random 80%/10%/10% train/validation/test split, repeated 100 times, mean±SD reported; evaluated separately on NYU and UM single-site cohorts (no leave-site-out or pooled multi-site evaluation)
charting.dataset_openly_available: Partly — data availability statement refers to article/supplementary material and further inquiries to corresponding author; no code repository link found

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction study; ABIDE I single-site cohorts, NYU (184 subjects: 79 ASD, 105 NC, primary) and UM (secondary)
narrative_row.methods: DPARSF-preprocessed resting-state fMRI, multi-scale functional connectivity networks built from AAL (116 ROIs) and CC200 (200 ROIs) atlases, classified with a multi-scale graph convolutional network (MGRL) with feature fusion; evaluated with a repeated random 80/10/10 split (100 repeats)
narrative_row.outcomes: MGRL outperformed single-scale GCN and handcrafted-feature baselines on both sites (NYU accuracy 0.795, AUC 0.886; UM accuracy 0.762, AUC 0.867), with multi-scale atlas fusion improving performance by at least 3% over single-atlas GCNs
narrative_row.key_limitations: Restricted to single sites to avoid inter-site heterogeneity rather than modelling it; no leave-site-out or pooled multi-site evaluation; diagnostic instrument/criteria and motion QC threshold not described; data availability limited to a general statement with no code link
narrative_row.relevance_notes: Demonstrates an atlas-fusion GCN approach validated with a repeated-split uncertainty estimate on two separate ABIDE single-site subsets, explicitly avoiding rather than addressing multi-site heterogeneity.
